glance_takeaway: This is a decision brief recommending a vector-search engine for Fernwick's search platform. The recommendation is conditional, not a flat winner: pick Hearth (self-hosted) if an approved infra hire and a 4-engineer on-call rotation are locked in by Oct 1, 2026; otherwise fall back to Quiver (managed SaaS) with a mandatory, budgeted exit plan. Two of four candidates were eliminated on must-have failures — including the one with the best raw benchmarks — and cost ranking inverts with scale (Quiver cheapest at 1M vectors, most expensive at 10M/100M), with a standing override to Quiver if filtered-query share exceeds 60% or facet selectivity drops below ~2%.

F1.note: Must-have chips M1-M5 with thresholds; tooltips carry the full definitions (e.g. M1 'p95 <= 100 ms at 10M... including the 30% filtered traffic', M3 'down to 5% selectivity').

F2.note: Stat strip: '4.1M vectors today, x2/yr', '30% of queries filtered, rising'; cost tabs label '10M — 12 mo' and '100M — 4-5 yr'.

F3.note: Collapsed 'How the numbers were produced' details: 2026-06-08 -> 06-19, frozen 10M snapshot, identical 3-node allocation for self-hosted, 48-hour log replayed at 120 QPS, recall vs exact brute-force. Reachable, not at rest.

F4.note: Matrix row 'p95 latency, unfiltered': 18/41/95/12 ms; pgnearest marked '~' (marginal but passing), Braid bolded fastest.

F5.note: Matrix row 'Recall@10, unfiltered (M2)': 0.97 / 0.94 / 0.89 x / 0.98; only pgnearest flagged as failing.

F6.note: pgnearest card badge 'Eliminated — fails M1 + M2' with '110 ms filtered x (budget 100) . 0.89 recall x (floor 0.92)'; matrix verdict FAIL (M1, M2).

F7.note: Braid card: 'Fastest and highest recall in the bakeoff — and it doesn't matter'; deep dive: 'no native filtered search... 0.71 at 5% — far below M3's 0.90 floor. Structural, not tunable.'

F8.note: Hearth deep dive: '0.90 at 5% selectivity — exactly at the M3 floor; degraded to 0.86 at 1%'; Quiver deep dive: 'held 0.95 even at 1%'; matrix shows '0.90 ~ (at floor)'.

F9.note: Matrix 'Cost @1M' row: $180 (best) / $520 / $240 / $210; 1M cost tab shows Quiver cheapest badge.

F10.note: Matrix @10M $1,900 vs $1,400 (both check M5) and @100M $23,000 vs $6,800; 100M panel caption 'Quiver is 3.4x Hearth'; pgnearest ~$13,500 (est.), Braid ~$4,200 (est. + DIY build) marked as estimates.

F11.note: Callouts: 'Infra-only crossover: ~3M vectors — already behind us' and 'Labor-adjusted crossover: ~30M vectors — around 2029'; labor toggle labeled '~0.2 FTE steady-state ~ +$2,800/mo loaded'.

F12.note: Quiver deep dive 'effectively 0 FTE; vendor on-call; 99.9% SLA'; Hearth deep dive '~0.5 FTE first quarter... settling to ~0.2 FTE, plus a >=4-engineer on-call rotation. Req PLAT-7... approved, not yet filled.'

F13.note: Quiver deep dive: proprietary DSL, exit '~3 engineer-weeks today, growing'; 'In-VPC deployment is not offered, ever'; 'Why Hearth first' ties in-VPC to 2027 enterprise-seller contracts; Hearth 'Lock-in: low', in-VPC.

F14.note: Decision rail IF/OTHERWISE with both dated conditions; 'The Quiver fallback comes with teeth' lists SearchIndex adapter, quarterly export drill into scratch Hearth cluster, ~3 engineer-week budget, re-evaluate at 30M or first renewal.

F15.note: Standing-override rail card: '>60% of traffic, or... selectivity drops below ~2%: Quiver regardless'; dates line 'Headcount checkpoint 2026-10-01 . full decision review 2027-01-15'.

strengths: The above-the-fold glance zone alone carries the full decision structure: conditional IF/OTHERWISE/OVERRIDE rail with dates, elimination-vs-tradeoff framing, cost inversion, and the 'benchmark winner fails a must-have' point.

Fact fidelity is essentially perfect: all 15 ground-truth facts present with correct numbers and directionality, estimates flagged as estimates, and Hearth's zero-margin M3 pass stated plainly rather than smoothed over.
Progressive disclosure is disciplined: cards summarize, deep dives carry the long tail; the cost explorer rests on the decision-relevant 10M view; methodology is available but out of the way.

The 'What would change your mind?' flips section directly serves the brief's reading goal of defending the decision under attack, with quantified flip conditions (e.g. 25% repricing moves the crossover to ~20M).
Caveats survive: renewal not price-locked, SLA recourse limited to credits, Braid's 100M figure excludes a DIY build, pgnearest v1.0 undated.
weaknesses: Bars rescale within each cost tab ('bars scale within each view'), so cross-scale magnitude comparison is not visual — the reader must read labels; a shared-axis or line view would show the crossover shape rather than assert it in callout prose.
No table of contents or in-page navigation on a long single scroll; wayfinding relies on scanning h2 headings.
Several load-bearing definitions (M1's 'including filtered traffic', selectivity, FTE) live only in hover/focus tooltips, which are fragile on touch and invisible in print.
Crossover specifics (~3M past, ~30M/~2029) do not land at glance — they sit mid-page in callouts; a time-pressed director reading only the fold misses T3's sharpest numbers.
Density is at the ceiling for the audience: the glance zone alone has ~5 chips, a 3-cell rail, and 4 stat-heavy cards; a less motivated reader could stall before the cost section.
evaluator_notes: Accuracy 10.0 is formula-driven: 15/15 facts conveyed, 0 distorted, 0 contradicted (10 x 15/15). Glance scored from the recorded takeaway: T2 and T4 fully landed, T1 landed minus the explicit tradeoff axes, T3 landed minus crossover locations — 8.5, not 10. Interactive content (deep dives, cost tabs, labor toggle, methodology) was credited for depth only; the resting state (10M infra-only view, collapsed cards) was judged for glance. Rendering verified in both screenshots; the no-JS fallback (all panels visible, tabs hidden) is a sound progressive-enhancement choice. Overall = 0.35*10.0 + 0.30*8.5 + 0.15*8.5 + 0.10*8.0 + 0.10*8.0 = 8.925 -> 8.9.
